announce-release.purpose: Prepare release announcements from release evidence
announce-release.when: A version has actually been published and users or teammates need to know what changed.
announce-release.provide: The published Release Package, actual release outcome, audience and channels; delivery also needs authorization.
announce-release.use: Use announce-release to draft an announcement for the named audience from the published result. Show me the draft first.
announce-release.result: Audience-specific drafts. A delivery receipt exists only after authorized sending through an available tool; a draft is not a sent announcement.
announce-release.name: announce-release

archive-milestone.purpose: Archive completed milestones and preserve evidence
archive-milestone.when: A phase, version or time period needs archiving, or the roadmap history has become too long.
archive-milestone.provide: The archive scope, original records, completion evidence and project archiving conventions.
archive-milestone.use: Use archive-milestone to preview an archive plan for this scope, preserving unfinished work and existing links.
archive-milestone.result: A source-backed archive snapshot or preview. Archiving does not mark unfinished work complete; writes stay within authorization.
archive-milestone.name: archive-milestone

assess-product-opportunity.when: Product opportunity analysis already has research evidence and needs an internal assessment of whether to continue.
assess-product-opportunity.provide: Research reports, user signals, opportunity scope and constraints, including missing evidence.
assess-product-opportunity.use: Use product-opportunity-analysis to assess this opportunity from the research. Let it coordinate assess-product-opportunity instead of invoking that internal step directly.
assess-product-opportunity.result: Evidence-backed advice to proceed, explore, defer or stop. It neither grants business approval nor rewrites the research.
assess-product-opportunity.name: assess-product-opportunity

automate-tests.when: You want to run existing project tests but do not know the correct commands or environment limits.
automate-tests.provide: Repository path, quick or full test scope, and permission boundaries for dependencies, network and services.
automate-tests.use: Use automate-tests to find test commands in project documentation/configuration, run the permitted tests and report results.
automate-tests.result: Actual commands, pass/fail records, skipped checks and logs. It does not write tests or repair failures.
automate-tests.name: automate-tests

capture-work-items.purpose: Capture requirements and issues as work items
capture-work-items.when: You have a requirement, defect or issue to record formally before deeper work.
capture-work-items.provide: The original description, project, related strategic goal and document location; missing information can be clarified.
capture-work-items.use: Use capture-work-items to record this description as a structured work item, checking missing required information first.
capture-work-items.result: A local work-item document and path. Capture does not automatically set priority or replace full requirements review.
capture-work-items.name: capture-work-items

changelog-video.purpose: Make a changelog video from confirmed release material
changelog-video.when: A release has been decided and its confirmed changes need a short video.
changelog-video.provide: Confirmed changes, project/version, channel, scope, output directory and whether video is mandatory; optionally audience and assets.
changelog-video.use: Use changelog-video to make a release video from these confirmed changes, first checking assets and local rendering tools.
changelog-video.result: Video files and verification, or an explicit unavailable reason. It does not choose versions, create tags or publish videos.
changelog-video.name: changelog-video

commit-work.when: Local changes are ready and should become logically scoped Git commits.
commit-work.provide: Uncommitted repository changes, the intended scope and project check requirements.
commit-work.use: Use commit-work to check these changes and commit logical scopes after reviewing staged diffs and applicable checks.
commit-work.result: Local commits, messages and check results. It does not automatically push or create a pull request.
commit-work.name: commit-work

competitive-research.when: You need to compare competitors or alternatives without relying on marketing claims alone.
competitive-research.provide: Competitor set, comparison dimensions, region, versions/plans and an as-of date.
competitive-research.use: Use competitive-research to compare these competitors' capabilities, positioning and prices, separating verified facts from unknowns.
competitive-research.result: A dated, sourced comparison and research report. Undocumented does not mean a feature is absent.
competitive-research.name: competitive-research

consume-nats-message.purpose: Consume and handle NATS messages by contract
consume-nats-message.when: A consumer project needs to drain pending NATS messages.
consume-nats-message.provide: Consumer repository, message contract, producer or subject, batch size, available NATS tools and processing authorization.
consume-nats-message.use: Use consume-nats-message to process pending messages on the named subject under the project contract and summarize outcomes.
consume-nats-message.result: Acknowledgment, retry and termination statistics with error reasons; the report does not dump full message bodies.
consume-nats-message.name: consume-nats-message

decontextualize-text.purpose: Remove private context for standalone reuse
decontextualize-text.when: Text relies on internal company knowledge and must be reusable outside or by another team.
decontextualize-text.provide: Original text, readers, internal names to remove and meanings that must remain.
decontextualize-text.use: Use decontextualize-text to make this text understandable without internal background while preserving its logic.
decontextualize-text.result: Standalone text without internal dependencies, retaining structure, logic and capability boundaries.
decontextualize-text.name: decontextualize-text

deep-research.when: An open question needs investigation, with evidence and uncertainty made clear.
deep-research.provide: Research question, purpose, scope, as-of date and permitted sources.
deep-research.use: Use deep-research to investigate this question and cross-check sources, separating facts, claims, inferences and unknowns.
deep-research.result: Cited findings and a structured research record. It does not make the product decision for you.
deep-research.name: deep-research

define-docs-norms.when: A reviewed documentation proposal needs to become the project's formal conventions.
define-docs-norms.provide: The approved proposal, existing norms file and the scope to create, merge or replace.
define-docs-norms.use: Use define-docs-norms to update documentation conventions from the reviewed proposal, preserving unrelated content.
define-docs-norms.result: The project's docs/ARTIFACT_NORMS.md and change explanation. It does not decide every convention from scratch.
define-docs-norms.name: define-docs-norms

define-mission.when: The project's reason for existing is unclear and the team needs a shared purpose.
define-mission.provide: What the project does, whom it serves, the problem it solves and existing introductions.
define-mission.use: Use define-mission to clarify why this project exists and save the mission in the agreed location.
define-mission.result: A concise mission statement and document: why we do this, rather than a replacement for vision or roadmap.
define-mission.name: define-mission

define-north-star.purpose: Define a metric for core user value
define-north-star.when: Many metrics exist, but it is unclear which best represents the value users receive.
define-north-star.provide: Product, target users, core value, mission or vision; optionally existing metrics.
define-north-star.use: Use define-north-star to derive one North Star Metric for core user value, explaining its definition and limitations.
define-north-star.result: One primary metric definition, rationale and necessary supporting metrics. It does not invent actual measurements.
define-north-star.name: define-north-star

define-roadmap.purpose: Design roadmap structure or populate a settled layout
define-roadmap.when: You need roadmap structure, content on an agreed structure, or alignment of an existing plan.
define-roadmap.provide: Whether scope is structure, content or both; project conventions, existing plans and goals. Content planning also needs requirement/defect sources.
define-roadmap.use: Use define-roadmap within the requested scope, preserving existing decisions, timing commitments and links.
define-roadmap.result: The scoped structure or source-backed plan. Structure-only work does not invent business scheduling.
define-roadmap.name: define-roadmap

define-strategic-pillars.purpose: Turn vision into a few strategic themes
define-strategic-pillars.when: Vision and a core metric exist, but focused themes are needed to guide later goals.
define-strategic-pillars.provide: Vision, North Star Metric and project context; optionally existing pillars and organizational constraints.
define-strategic-pillars.use: Use define-strategic-pillars to derive strategic pillars from vision and the North Star Metric, explaining how they support direction.
define-strategic-pillars.result: Three to five strategic themes with short explanations, rather than a detailed task list.
define-strategic-pillars.name: define-strategic-pillars

define-vision.purpose: Describe the future the project aims to create
define-vision.when: The purpose is clear and you need a long-term picture of the future to create.
define-vision.provide: Mission and project context; optionally existing vision, readers and time horizon.
define-vision.use: Use define-vision to define a long-term vision aligned with the mission and save it in the agreed location.
define-vision.result: A one-to-three-sentence vision with necessary explanation. It describes a future state rather than scheduling development.
define-vision.name: define-vision

deliver-feature.purpose: Deliver a feature branch into the main branch
deliver-feature.when: One feature branch is complete in a linked worktree and needs merging into main and pushing.
deliver-feature.provide: A clean linked worktree, a non-main branch, target main branch, push authorization and cleanup choice.
deliver-feature.use: Use deliver-feature to merge the current feature branch into main, push it and handle the worktree according to my choice.
deliver-feature.result: Merge commit, push result and optional cleanup result. This does not establish that the product was released.
deliver-feature.name: deliver-feature

design-strategic-goals.purpose: Design long-term goals that advance the vision
design-strategic-goals.when: Direction is agreed and you need to define the changes to achieve over the long term.
design-strategic-goals.provide: Project context, vision and North Star Metric; optionally existing goals, time horizon and constraints.
design-strategic-goals.use: Use design-strategic-goals to create goals aligned with vision and the North Star Metric, preserving settled direction.
design-strategic-goals.result: A document with three to five long-term goals; missing upstream material is identified through repository-grounded assumptions.
design-strategic-goals.name: design-strategic-goals

generate-agent-entry.purpose: Write the agent's project entry instructions
generate-agent-entry.when: Agents entering the project need to know what it is and what to read first.
generate-agent-entry.provide: Project identity, asset directories, authoritative material, adopted workflows and existing AGENTS.md.
generate-agent-entry.use: Use generate-agent-entry to write or revise this project's AGENTS.md and verify every loading entry.
generate-agent-entry.result: An agent entry file, checklist and verification results. Review-only scope reports issues without changing files.
generate-agent-entry.name: generate-agent-entry

generate-github-workflow.when: Tests, builds or release checks need to run through GitHub Actions.
generate-github-workflow.provide: Purpose, language versions, package manager, actual build/test commands, triggers and output path.
generate-github-workflow.use: Use generate-github-workflow with the project's real commands, explaining permissions, pinned versions and remaining configuration.
generate-github-workflow.result: Workflow YAML and setup notes. Generated files do not prove a remote workflow has run.
generate-github-workflow.name: generate-github-workflow

generate-standard-readme.purpose: Create a concise, useful project README
generate-standard-readme.when: Repository visitors cannot tell what it is or where to begin.
generate-standard-readme.provide: Project name, one-line explanation, real usage/entry points, license and existing docs.
generate-standard-readme.use: Use generate-standard-readme to organize a concise README explaining the project's purpose and starting point.
generate-standard-readme.result: A root README and valid entry links, keeping only sections useful to readers.
generate-standard-readme.name: generate-standard-readme

integrate-branches.purpose: Integrate selected branches and clean worktrees
integrate-branches.when: Several branches or linked worktrees need integrating into main one by one.
integrate-branches.provide: The primary repository on main, candidate branches/worktrees, selected scope and push authorization.
integrate-branches.use: Use integrate-branches to list candidates for my selection, then merge/push them in order and clean successfully integrated worktrees.
integrate-branches.result: Per-branch merge, push and cleanup outcomes. Failures remain explicit; partial success is not reported as full completion.
integrate-branches.name: integrate-branches

manage-secret.purpose: Manage personal credentials in the local Keychain
manage-secret.when: A credential on your personal Mac needs storing, lookup, rotation or deletion.
manage-secret.provide: Project, environment, credential type, account and operation. Never put real secrets in this page or ordinary examples; use controlled input for storage.
manage-secret.use: Use manage-secret to manage the named credential in this Mac's Keychain, checking the entry first and hiding secret values in feedback.
manage-secret.result: A local Keychain entry and operation result. Secrets are not echoed; team vaults and cross-machine sync are outside scope.
manage-secret.name: manage-secret

map-item-dependencies.when: Work is prioritized but its prerequisites or start conditions are unclear.
map-item-dependencies.provide: Backlog, current roadmap, required deliverables and need-by dates; optionally a bounded scope.
map-item-dependencies.use: Use map-item-dependencies to identify these items' dependencies, readiness conditions and ways to reduce blockers.
map-item-dependencies.result: Dependency map, need-by schedule, blockers and item records. It does not replace priority decisions.
map-item-dependencies.name: map-item-dependencies

market-research.purpose: Research markets, demand, customers and size
market-research.when: You need evidence about a market's customers, demand, changes or size.
market-research.provide: Region, users and buyers, included/excluded products, period and currency.
market-research.use: Use market-research to investigate this market's demand and size, explaining estimates and evidence gaps.
market-research.result: Sourced market research and reproducible estimates. Insufficient evidence is explicitly reported rather than supporting a size claim.
market-research.name: market-research

orchestrate-code-review.when: A change set needs a combined review from applicable engineering perspectives.
orchestrate-code-review.provide: Diff or directory scope, project languages/frameworks and relevant conventions; optionally specific concerns.
orchestrate-code-review.use: Use orchestrate-code-review to select applicable engineering reviews for these changes and aggregate findings, explaining skipped steps.
orchestrate-code-review.result: Engineering findings, risks and coverage grouped by location. This does not establish requirements alignment or actual acceptance.
orchestrate-code-review.name: orchestrate-code-review

orchestrate-governance-step.when: The next governance action has been diagnosed and should advance safely one step.
orchestrate-governance-step.provide: Project governance document location; optionally the latest plan-next recommendation and existing authorization.
orchestrate-governance-step.use: Use orchestrate-governance-step to recheck current governance state, advance only one eligible action and report whether to continue.
orchestrate-governance-step.result: One action's outcome or a reason to wait, ask or stop. It does not unconditionally run an entire project workflow.
orchestrate-governance-step.name: orchestrate-governance-step

orchestrate-repair-loop.purpose: Repair implementation and recheck both quality gates
orchestrate-repair-loop.when: Implementation has review findings or failing tests and needs targeted repair and repeated verification.
orchestrate-repair-loop.provide: Implementation scope, approved requirements/designs, findings, test methods, environment limits and iteration cap.
orchestrate-repair-loop.use: Use orchestrate-repair-loop to repair these issues and recheck engineering quality, functional alignment and actual verification.
orchestrate-repair-loop.result: Per-round repair/review records, remaining issues or stop reasons. Missing business decisions are not invented.
orchestrate-repair-loop.name: orchestrate-repair-loop

orchestrate-repair-requirements-loop.purpose: Repair and re-review an existing requirement
orchestrate-repair-requirements-loop.when: An existing requirement has issues that need evidence-grounded repair and re-review.
orchestrate-repair-requirements-loop.provide: Requirement document, authoritative business material and findings; optionally repair scope and stop conditions.
orchestrate-repair-requirements-loop.use: Use orchestrate-repair-requirements-loop to review and repair this requirement, then re-review it; stop and explain unresolved business trade-offs.
orchestrate-repair-requirements-loop.result: A revised requirement and round-by-round review records, rather than jumping straight to design or implementation.
orchestrate-repair-requirements-loop.name: orchestrate-repair-requirements-loop

orchestrate-roadmap-planning.purpose: Coordinate roadmap structure, content and alignment
orchestrate-roadmap-planning.when: You are unsure which capabilities this round of roadmap work needs.
orchestrate-roadmap-planning.provide: The goal: structure, content, continuous planning or existing-plan alignment; current documents and decisions.
orchestrate-roadmap-planning.use: Use orchestrate-roadmap-planning to coordinate applicable roadmap capabilities for this goal, retaining settled priorities, commitments and links.
orchestrate-roadmap-planning.result: A summary of applicable steps and roadmap changes. It does not rerun everything; update-roadmap can handle status/date maintenance.
orchestrate-roadmap-planning.name: orchestrate-roadmap-planning

plan-next.purpose: Diagnose governance state and suggest the next step
plan-next.when: You want to know the most useful governance action to advance now.
plan-next.provide: Governance document location and current evidence; optionally which recommendation to skip and for how long.
plan-next.use: Use plan-next to read the current project state and recommend the next action with its reason and completion signal.
plan-next.result: Evidence-backed recommendations and blockers. It does not execute them by default or replace task-state tracking.
plan-next.name: plan-next

policy-research.purpose: Research policy applicability and product impact
policy-research.when: A jurisdiction's policy may affect the product and its official text and timing need checking.
policy-research.provide: Jurisdiction, affected activities/entities, question, relevant period and as-of date.
policy-research.use: Use policy-research to verify official policy text, effective dates and applicability, explaining possible product implications.
policy-research.result: An official-source research report and unresolved items, not a legal conclusion or compliance certification.
policy-research.name: policy-research

prepare-presales-response.when: A presales questionnaire or customer inquiry needs grounded, reusable answers.
prepare-presales-response.provide: Original questions, audience, product scope, available evidence, earlier confirmations and delivery format.
prepare-presales-response.use: Use prepare-presales-response to draft answers from verifiable product material, separating missing evidence and customer-specific terms.
prepare-presales-response.result: Evidence-backed drafts, supporting material and reusable product knowledge. Unknown capabilities are not turned into promises.
prepare-presales-response.name: prepare-presales-response

prepare-release.purpose: Build and validate a Release Package
prepare-release.when: You want to decide whether this work merits a release and prepare complete release material.
prepare-release.provide: Repository, comparison baseline, version policy, channel, candidate artifacts and project check requirements.
prepare-release.use: Use prepare-release to inspect changes and prepare a Release Package, first confirming the release decision and required artifacts.
prepare-release.result: A release/no-release decision record, change list and readiness checks. It does not publish or send announcements.
prepare-release.name: prepare-release

prioritize-backlog.purpose: Prioritize backlog items under project policy
prioritize-backlog.when: A large backlog contains items whose priorities have not been settled.
prioritize-backlog.provide: Work items and project priority policy; reassessment needs explicit scope/evidence and impact/cost facts.
prioritize-backlog.use: Use prioritize-backlog to prioritize unsettled items under project policy, preserving settled decisions.
prioritize-backlog.result: A priority comparison and source-record updates. It does not schedule items on the roadmap or change dates.
prioritize-backlog.name: prioritize-backlog

product-opportunity-analysis.purpose: Coordinate research into a product opportunity package
product-opportunity-analysis.when: A product or feature opportunity needs several research perspectives and decision material.
product-opportunity-analysis.provide: Opportunity question, target users, region/time scope, existing material and allowed research scope.
product-opportunity-analysis.use: Use product-opportunity-analysis to coordinate relevant research, connecting evidence, counterevidence and a validation plan.
product-opportunity-analysis.result: A traceable Opportunity Package and recommendation. Producing material is not business approval.
product-opportunity-analysis.name: product-opportunity-analysis

promote-roadmap-items.purpose: Promote prioritized, ready work into the roadmap
promote-roadmap-items.when: Prioritized work needs a decision about near-term or later placement.
promote-roadmap-items.provide: Current roadmap, settled work-item priorities, strategic goals, dependencies and readiness evidence.
promote-roadmap-items.use: Use promote-roadmap-items to place these items into Now, Next or Later using settled priorities and readiness.
promote-roadmap-items.result: Placement/tier-change decisions and roadmap updates, preserving existing version scope and timing commitments without rescoring.
promote-roadmap-items.name: promote-roadmap-items

publish-nats-message.purpose: Publish NATS messages under a cross-team contract
publish-nats-message.when: A producer project needs to send another team a contract-compliant NATS message.
publish-nats-message.provide: Producer repository, event/subject, payload, contract and broker publish authorization; connected tools must be available.
publish-nats-message.use: Use publish-nats-message to verify this event's contract, publish this message and record the actual receipt.
publish-nats-message.result: A verified publication result. A missing contract is drafted and confirmed first; drafts are not sent messages.
publish-nats-message.name: publish-nats-message

publish-release.purpose: Validate a ready package and publish a release
publish-release.when: The Release Package is ready and an actual release is now required.
publish-release.provide: Ready Release Package, channel/provider, required check results and authorization for this release.
publish-release.use: Use publish-release to preview and validate this package, then perform publication only with authorization for this release.
publish-release.result: Actual tags, artifacts and provider receipts or failure details. Default preview is never reported as publication.
publish-release.name: publish-release

redeploy-local.purpose: Detect build/deployment setup and update local runtime
redeploy-local.when: Code changed and the project already running on this machine needs updating.
redeploy-local.provide: Project directory, existing build/deployment configuration and authorization to run the services and commands.
redeploy-local.use: Use redeploy-local to identify build/deployment from project evidence, update the local runtime and check health.
redeploy-local.result: Actual build, restart and health outcomes. Ambiguity is reported before acting rather than guessing commands.
redeploy-local.name: redeploy-local

refine-skill-design.purpose: Review and improve skill design and organization
refine-skill-design.when: Existing skills are hard to execute or poorly organized and need review or improvement.
refine-skill-design.provide: Explicit skill files/set, review/change scope and whether to edit in place or save a draft.
refine-skill-design.use: Use refine-skill-design to review and improve these skills' boundaries, instructions and local resources.
refine-skill-design.result: Skill revisions or drafts, reasons and version advice. Already-compliant skills remain unchanged.
refine-skill-design.name: refine-skill-design

review-architecture.purpose: Review module ownership, dependencies and contracts
review-architecture.when: Structural changes may complicate module boundaries, dependency direction or contracts.
review-architecture.provide: Selected files, directories or diff and relevant architecture conventions.
review-architecture.use: Use review-architecture to check boundaries, dependency direction, coupling and contract stability; report findings and unreviewed scope only.
review-architecture.result: Findings with locations, evidence and impact, or explicit no-findings and coverage notes. It does not repair/rewrite or imply other checks passed.
review-architecture.name: review-architecture

review-codebase.purpose: Review code organization and technical debt
review-codebase.when: You need to understand organization problems and technical debt in existing code.
review-codebase.provide: One or more directories/files; optionally important modules and specific concerns.
review-codebase.use: Use review-codebase to check organization, cross-module dependencies and interface stability; report findings and unreviewed scope only.
review-codebase.result: Findings with locations, evidence and impact, or explicit no-findings and coverage notes. It does not repair/rewrite or imply other checks passed.
review-codebase.name: review-codebase

review-diff.purpose: Review this diff's correctness and impact
review-diff.when: You want to know whether these changes introduce defects or regressions.
review-diff.provide: Current branch staged/unstaged diffs and untracked files within scope.
review-diff.use: Use review-diff to check correctness, compatibility and side effects; report findings and unreviewed scope only.
review-diff.result: Findings with locations, evidence and impact, or explicit no-findings and coverage notes. It does not repair/rewrite or imply other checks passed.
review-diff.name: review-diff

review-dotnet.when: Selected C# or F# code needs a language/runtime usage review.
review-dotnet.provide: Selected code/diff, .NET version and project conventions.
review-dotnet.use: Use review-dotnet to check async, nullability, disposal, API versioning and testability; report findings and unreviewed scope only.
review-dotnet.result: Findings with locations, evidence and impact, or explicit no-findings and coverage notes. It does not repair/rewrite or imply other checks passed.
review-dotnet.name: review-dotnet

review-error-surfacing.purpose: Review error detection and actionable messages
review-error-surfacing.when: Failures are swallowed, detected too late or reported without an actionable message.
review-error-surfacing.provide: Selected code and its input boundaries; optionally detection-layer and false-positive policies.
review-error-surfacing.use: Use review-error-surfacing to check untrusted input, failure detection boundaries and actionable messages; report findings and unreviewed scope only.
review-error-surfacing.result: Findings with locations, evidence and impact, or explicit no-findings and coverage notes. It does not repair/rewrite or imply other checks passed.
review-error-surfacing.name: review-error-surfacing

review-functional-design.purpose: Review functional design completeness and executability
review-functional-design.when: A functional design exists and needs checking before technical design begins.
review-functional-design.provide: Functional design, upstream requirement and relevant local conventions.
review-functional-design.use: Use review-functional-design to review this design against its Spec and quality Rule; report findings and unreviewed scope only.
review-functional-design.result: Findings with locations, evidence and impact, or explicit no-findings and coverage notes. It does not repair/rewrite or imply other checks passed.
review-functional-design.name: review-functional-design

relationships.title: Why we exist and where we are heading
relationships.body: Mission explains why the project exists; vision describes its intended future. Existing direction can be reused rather than redefined each time.

relationships.title: How to tell whether it helps
relationships.body: The North Star Metric reflects core user value. Strategic pillars group the direction into themes; goals describe the intended change.

relationships.title: Goals help select work
relationships.body: A goal can relate to several requirements or defects. Capturing them in the backlog does not place all of them on the roadmap or authorize implementation.

relationships.title: New evidence can come back
relationships.body: Research and user feedback can change goals, or just one work item or plan. Revisit only the affected part.

direction.summary: Direction explains why; goals describe the change we want. They help judge worthwhile work and can be revisited with new evidence.
direction.boundary: Reuse existing material. Roadmap placement, execution approval, acceptance and publication are distinct. Diagnosis/orchestration selects appropriate steps rather than restarting the whole chain.
direction.prompt: Use existing project material to identify users, core problems and current goals. Separate facts from inferences; draft goals and measures, preserve settled direction and list trade-offs I must decide.

help.line: Connect goals, backlog, dependencies and roadmap; update only affected plans when things change.
help.plane: Preserve settled decisions and commitments as the shared basis for planning.

usage.ordinary: Discussing which of two items comes first or adding a known date can be handled directly.
usage.cortex: Use applicable planning/maintenance methods when project policy, dependencies and existing commitments need systematic checking.
usage.adopted: Already-adopted project Specs and Rules still apply; they need not be manually invoked in every conversation.

assets.purpose: A method for a concrete task, such as reviewing an existing requirement.
What an artifact must contain, such as a requirement's objective and acceptance criteria.
Individually checkable quality constraints, such as acceptance criteria being verifiable.
How participants cooperate and hand work over; consult it when collaboration requires it.

relationships.title: Capture candidate work first
relationships.body: A backlog holds requirements and defects, including unscheduled work. Goals explain why an item merits consideration.

relationships.title: Important does not mean ready
relationships.body: Priority answers what matters more; dependencies identify missing conditions. Reuse decisions, fill gaps or perform explicitly requested reassessment.

relationships.title: Place work on the roadmap
relationships.body: Promotion uses priority and dependency readiness to choose Now/Next/Later. Roadmap placement does not approve implementation.

relationships.title: Definition and maintenance have different jobs
relationships.body: Roadmap definition owns structure and source-backed content. Maintenance updates existing status, dates and scope; it does not promote between Now/Next/Later.

relationships.title: Orchestration chooses a route as needed
relationships.body: Orchestration need not reprioritize the backlog or call maintenance. Structure-only work, content population, continuous planning and maintenance are different requests.

planning.summary: The goal is finding past requests. Search and reminders are both candidates; this example selects search because its conditions are ready.
planning.boundary: Reuse existing material. Roadmap placement, execution approval, acceptance and publication are distinct. Diagnosis/orchestration selects appropriate steps rather than restarting the whole chain.
planning.prompt: Plan a source-backed roadmap round from current direction, goals, requirements and defects. Preserve settled decisions/commitments and list trade-offs I must decide.

help.line: Research informs opportunities, goals and candidate work.
help.plane: Separate facts, inferences and gaps to support evidence-grounded trade-offs.

usage.ordinary: Explaining a concept or clarifying a question can be ordinary conversation.
usage.cortex: Use research methods when conclusions need sources, dates, evidence limitations or opportunity assessment.
usage.adopted: Already-adopted project Specs and Rules still apply; they need not be manually invoked in every conversation.

How participants cooperate and hand work over; consult it when collaboration requires it.

research.summary: A user says: “I cannot find my earlier requests.” Understand the difficulty first, then decide whether a change merits investment.
research.boundary: Research supplies facts and opportunity assessment interprets them; unverified assumptions do not become product decisions.
research.prompt: Investigate this question from existing material, separate facts/inferences/gaps and advise whether further investment makes sense. Do not decide unresolved product trade-offs for me.

help.line: Check requirements, designs and tasks against each other; return to the affected artifact when something is missing.

relationships.title: Writing an explanation differs from reviewing it
relationships.body: Project work produces requirements, designs and tasks. These review skills inspect existing material; they cannot invent missing business decisions.

relationships.title: Return to the unclear part
relationships.body: Fill requirement gaps in requirements, design issues in designs and missing tasks in tasks. Then recheck affected explanations and implementation.

design.summary: What does search include? What happens with no matches? Clarify those questions before coding, then check for omissions.
design.boundary: These skills review existing artifacts; they do not automatically produce every design. Project workflows create the artifacts; findings return to the relevant material for repair and re-review.
design.prompt: First ask directly about unclear parts of the existing requirement and update them, leaving business trade-offs for me. Follow adopted conventions; use relevant AI Cortex Specs, Rules or Skills when structure/review warrants them, without forcing a workflow on every conversation.

help.line: Repair identified issues, then recheck affected checks.
help.plane: Engineering quality, approved intent and actual acceptance each need their own evidence; none substitutes for another.

usage.ordinary: Pointing out an error or discussing a correction can happen directly.
usage.cortex: Use review methods and quality constraints when systematic engineering review, alignment and traceable rechecks are needed.
usage.adopted: Already-adopted project Specs and Rules still apply; they need not be manually invoked in every conversation.

relationships.title: Engineering review
relationships.body: Check correctness, structure and applicable quality constraints of the code itself. Finding no code issues does not prove the intended user need was met.

relationships.title: Alignment with intent
relationships.body: Compare implementation with approved requirements, designs and tasks to detect drift.

relationships.title: Actual acceptance
relationships.body: Run real user paths and compare outcomes with expectations. Repair identified issues and repeat affected review and verification.

quality.summary: Is the code sound? Does it do what was intended? Does it work in use? Check all three.
quality.boundary: Engineering and functional checks are parallel gates; neither replaces the other. Select language/framework/quality lenses by the diff; review does not replace running acceptance paths.
quality.prompt: Run applicable engineering review, separately check alignment with approved intent and execute necessary tests/acceptance. Repair blocking findings, recheck affected gates and report remaining limits.

help.line: Connect authorized tasks, code changes and actual runtime outcomes.
help.plane: Reuse project test/run conventions to reduce repeated guesses during handoff.

usage.ordinary: The current agent can explain code, implement changes or discuss errors directly.
usage.cortex: Use the relevant skills/conventions to discover tests, scaffold agent tests from an existing contract or update the local environment.
usage.adopted: Already-adopted project Specs and Rules still apply; they need not be manually invoked in every conversation.

relationships.title: A commit saves one version
relationships.body: Check scope, staged diff and applicable checks, then leave a clear commit. Work may be saved more than once.

relationships.title: Integration is a separate action
relationships.body: Merge and push under project branch, verification and authorization conventions. Neither saving nor merging proves users received a release.

commit.summary: Save only related changes and explain what changed and why. Integrate the branch into main when needed.
commit.boundary: Committing differs from pushing; integration differs from release. Single-branch delivery and multi-branch integration are alternative entries, not mandatory consecutive steps. Writes/pushes follow current authorization.
commit.prompt: Check these changes and verification results, prepare logically scoped commits and perform only authorized commit operations after staged review. Explain branch/integration options when needed; do not present commits as a published release.

help.line: Check preparation, publication and announcement prerequisites separately; feedback can return to relevant work.

relationships.title: Release to users
relationships.body: A ready package, passing required checks and authorization for this release are needed to produce an actual release result.

relationships.title: Communicate actual facts
relationships.body: Announcements follow real release results; sending also needs communication scope and authorization. Feedback may return to goals or work.

release.summary: Prepare release material, publish under project conventions and explain the changes. Then listen for feedback: is finding requests easier now?
release.boundary: Preparation, publication and announcement have separate owners. Video is optional, not mandatory; without an actual receipt, do not claim publication.
release.prompt: First prepare release material under project conventions, checking version, scope, verification and optional artifacts. Report readiness. Publication and sending follow existing authorization; do not fabricate success before release.

goal-basis.label: Goal basis
goal-basis.condition: Planning compares candidates against existing strategic goals; it does not require redefining goals each time.

planning-design.label: Plan detail
planning-design.condition: When planned work needs elaboration, hand it to requirements, design and tasks. Now placement does not approve artifacts or require rewriting existing designs.

design-build.label: Task basis
design-build.condition: Approved technical design can be decomposed into implementation tasks. This line describes artifact handoff, not review skills writing all code.

design-quality.label: Intent check
design-quality.condition: Compare approved requirements/designs/tasks with implementation and evidence. Disclose missing approvals; drafts are not completion authority.

repair-feedback.label: Repair & retest
repair-feedback.condition: Repair engineering/functional findings, then recheck affected gates. Each supplies separate evidence; pause at the stop conditions.

quality-planning.label: New work back
quality-planning.condition: If a report actually requests new behavior or belongs to existing intake, return it with evidence to the backlog. Repair does not silently expand scope or change priority.

checks-release.label: Release checks
checks-release.condition: Reuse and record applicable test/build/review results during release preparation. Not every review runs every time, and passing checks does not authorize release.

history-release.label: Change evidence
history-release.condition: Release preparation uses repository history, target commits and scope; it does not require rerunning commit-work first.

conditional-commit.label: Commit if needed
conditional-commit.condition: Call commit-work only when the release tool does not commit itself. This return line is not a mandatory repeated commit; a commit is not publication.

norms-planning.label: Project norms
norms-planning.condition: Planning reads existing norms to choose locations, views and maintenance methods. Use norm-maintenance capabilities only when conventions need creating/changing; no forced reinitialization.

norms-collaboration.label: Shared norms
norms-collaboration.condition: Prepare responses using adopted authority/maintenance conventions. Keep product facts and customer terms separate without creating duplicate rules.

research-collaboration.label: Research support
research-collaboration.condition: Request research when communication raises a substantive investigation, then use its evidence in the response. Ordinary FAQ lookup does not need a research report. Two arrows mean request/result handoff, not a mandatory stage.

research-planning.label: Research input
research-planning.condition: Opportunity recommendations inform the owner's assessment of candidate work. Planning inclusion remains a separate decision; research does not automatically create requirements or approve a roadmap. This is artifact use, not research skills calling planning skills.

define-mission__define-vision.label: Mission input
define-mission__define-vision.condition: Mission content is needed; an existing mission can be reused without rerunning the skill.

define-vision__define-strategic-pillars.label: Vision input
define-vision__define-strategic-pillars.condition: Strategic pillars use vision and the North Star Metric; existing artifacts can be reused.

define-north-star__define-strategic-pill.label: Metric input
define-north-star__define-strategic-pill.condition: Use the core-value metric without necessarily redefining it.

define-vision__design-strategic-goals.label: Vision input
define-vision__design-strategic-goals.condition: Normally read the existing vision; if missing, the skill handles that from repository evidence.

define-north-star__design-strategic-goal.label: Metric input
define-north-star__design-strategic-goal.condition: Goals align with the existing core-value metric; upstream skills need not rerun.

prepare-release__publish-release.condition: Preparation must meet release prerequisites, with separate authorization for actual publication. Prepared is not published.

publish-release__announce-release.label: Actual release result
publish-release__announce-release.condition: Announcements use published facts and still need sending authorization; publication does not trigger automatic broadcast.

publish-release__commit-work.label: Commit by project method

design-strategic-goals__capture-work-ite.label: Link to goals
design-strategic-goals__capture-work-ite.condition: Link work items to existing strategic goals; recording an item does not require redefining goals.

design-strategic-goals__promote-roadmap-.label: Goals inform choices
design-strategic-goals__promote-roadmap-.condition: Compare candidates across goals. A goal link does not give each goal a fixed allocation.

prioritize-backlog__promote-roadmap-item.label: Priority input
prioritize-backlog__promote-roadmap-item.condition: Promotion reads settled priorities; assess only unsettled items or explicit reassessment requests.

map-item-dependencies__promote-roadmap-i.label: Dependency input

capture-work-items__prioritize-backlog.label: Work-item input
capture-work-items__prioritize-backlog.condition: Prioritize existing work items. Capturing an item does not score it automatically; settled priorities are not automatically reassessed.

requirement-loop.label: Review → revise → re-review
requirement-loop.condition: Repair one existing requirement from findings and re-review it. This does not require every design skill to run in turn.

quality-loop.label: Check → repair → recheck
quality-loop.condition: Repeat only checks affected by the repair, until convergence or a stop condition.

bug.title: A check finds a code issue.
bug.body: Return to implementation, repair it and recheck affected gates. Verification and clear commits can happen repeatedly during development.

requirements.title: An existing requirement omits search scope.
requirements.body: The agent can ask directly and update the requirement. Consult Specs, Rules or review skills when consistency/systematic checking is needed; do not restart every work item.

release.title: Preparing to deliver changes to users.
release.body: Check the package, required quality evidence and authorization first. Prepare announcements from actual release results; a commit does not replace that evidence.

direction.subtitle: Why we do this and what should change

build.subtitle: Build, test and revise when needed

pass.title: This set of checks passed.
pass.body: This example only assumes applicable checks completed. Saving, integration and release each still need their own scope/prerequisite checks.

fail.title: An issue needs repair.
fail.body: Repair identified issues and recheck affected areas. Do not ignore failures to hand work over.

missing.title: An actual check is still missing.
missing.body: Code that looks sound does not prove users can find their records. Gather actual verification evidence first.

foundation.label: Across topics: docs & conventions
foundation.condition: Apply the adopted project entry, authoritative sources and working agreements. Existing documentation norms constrain relevant artifacts; no rerun is implied.

collaboration.label: Across topics: communication & handoff
collaboration.condition: When handing material to another reader or team, make it understandable without private context. This is optional support, not a required step for every task.

map-planning.name: Direction & planning
map-planning.purpose: Connect everyday work to a project purpose.

map-delivery.name: Delivery & release
map-delivery.purpose: Move reviewed work into a usable release.

map-library.name: Project & asset maintenance
map-library.purpose: Keep reusable knowledge discoverable and usable.
